Since matter is of year 2012 and it is taken up for disposal with consent of learned counsel for parties.

2. Challenging impugned judgment and award dated 28.06.2011 passed by Court of District Judge (Fast Track) and MACT Haveri, in MVC no.30/2011, this appeal is filed by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: 3. Brief facts as stated are that on 04.04.2010, when claimant was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-27/J-5657 near D.C. Office, Haveri, a Santro car bearing registration no.MH- 04/CJ-8962, driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner and dashed against motorcycle and caused accident.
In said accident, he sustained grievous injuries.
Despite taking treatment at Government Hospital, Haveri, and Kshema Orthopaedic Centre at Hubli, he did not recover fully and sustained permanent physical disability.
Claiming compensation for same, claimant filed claim petition against owner and insurer of car under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
4. On service of notice, owner did not appear.
He was placed ex-parte.
Insurer opposed claim petition admitting insurance.
It denied liability on ground that driver of Santro car was intoxicated at time of accident.
He did not have valid and effective driving licence.
Thereafter, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimant as P.W.1 and Dr.Laxman Naik as P.W.2.
Exs. P.1 to 17 were marked.

In rebuttal, insurer was examined as R.W.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 and 2.
5.

On consideration, Tribunal held that accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver and claimant was entitled for compensation of Rs.2,00.000/- with interest at rate of 6% per annum from insurer.
Not satisfied with quantum of compensation claimant is in appeal.

6. Sri. Srinivas K. Nadamani, appearing for Sri.Jagadish Patil, learned counsel for claimant/appellant submitted that tribunal erred in not granting compensation towards 'future loss of earning', though claimant had sustained fracture of right femur and also fracture of right Tibia which were mal - united and compound fracture.
It was submitted that award of compensation under other heads were also grossly inadequate and sought for enhancement of compensation.
7. On other hand Sri. Suresh .S. Gundi, learned counsel for respondent/insurer sought to justify award and opposed appeal.
It was submitted that for fracture of femur and tibia, compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- on overall consideration is just and proper, did not calls for enhancement.
It was submitted that tribunal had rejected Income-tax return filed by claimant on ground that it was filed subsequent to date of accident.
Therefore, there was no loss of earning capacity.

2 8.
Heard learned counsel for parties, perused impugned judgment and award.
9. From above submission, only claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

Occurrence of accident due to rash and negligent riding of car by its driver and issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on date of accident and liability of insurer to pay compensation are not in dispute.

Only point that would arise of consideration is:
"Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
10.
Insofar so monthly income, claimant has stated that deceased was working as businessman in Garment sales and also doing agriculture, earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
To substantiate same, he had filed PAN card at Ex.P.8 and Income-tax Returns along with acknowledgments at Ex.P.9 to 11 respectively.

On perusal of Income-tax Returns (certified copy which were furnished by learned counsel for claimant) it is seen that Income-tax Returns for year 2010-11 was filed on 15.11.2010 i.e.
after date of accident.
However, Income-tax Returns for year 2009-10 was filed on 10.03.2010 gross income shown is Rs.1,41,842/-.
Even income tax returns for year 2008-09 would indicate income at Rs.1,20,047/-.

Profit and loss account accompanying returns would indicate that claimant was doing business in shop premises for which he would incur expenses and entire income cannot be treated as net profit.
11.
Notional income for year 2010 is Rs.5,500.
However claimant cannot be equated to that of an ordinary coolie.
Taking into account Income-tax Returns, it would be proper to consider monthly income of claimant at Rs.9,000/-.
Insofar as disability, claimant has produced wound certificate as per Ex.P.6, discharge summary Ex.P.7, disability certificate and X-ray Ex.P.15 to 17 respectively.
12. From Ex.P.16, it is seen that claimant sustained compound fracture of femur and upper shaft of right tibia with displacement.
Disability certificate would also indicate that implants insito.
Dri.Laman Naik, orthopedic surgeon at Government Hospital, Haveri is examined as P.W.2.
On examination of claimant, he has assessed limb disability at 65%, taking into account restriction of flections of right knee from 0 to 65 degree.

Considering occupation, assessment of disability to limb,
would require modification, while assessing 'loss of earning capacity'.
Therefore, it would appropriate to consider 15% as 'loss of earning capacity'.

Thus future loss of income would be as follows:
Rs.1,350 x 12 x 17 = Rs.2,75,400/-
13.
Thus, claimant has sustained two grievous fractures.
Considering same, tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/- towards 'pain and suffering', which would not be adequate, it would be proper to enhance it to Rs.40,000/-.
Tribunal has awarded Rs.20.000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
Considering restriction of movement of right knee and right hand, it would be appropriate to enhance it to Rs.30,000/-.
14. Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/- towards 'medical and other incidental expenses'.
After verifying bills since there is complete reimbursement, there is no scope for enhancement.

Tribunal has considered period of two months as lay off.
Normally, fractures takes about three months to heal.
Therefore 'loss of income during lay off period is to be enhanced to Rs.27,000/- and award of Rs.30,000/- towards disability would requires to be set aside, as future loss of income would be awarded.

Thus total compensation would be as follows:
Sl.no.
Heads Amount
1 Pain
and suffering 40,000/-

2 Medical and other 1,00,000/-
 incidental expenses

3 Loss of amenities 30,000/-
 4

Future loss of income 2,75,400/-
 5 Loss of income during 27,000/-
 lay off period  Total Rs.4,72,400/-
 16.
Point no.2 is answered partly in affirmative as above.

Consequently, I pass following:
 ORDER  a. Appeal is allowed in part.
 b. Claimant is held entitled for  reassessed compensation of  Rs.4,72,400/- as against Rs.2,00,000/- awarded by tribunal.
- 10 - c. Claimant would be entitled to interest at 6% per annum on enhanced compensation also.
d. Insurers are directed to deposit enhanced compensation within six weeks.
